fatal_errors: The proposed Nb ALD barrier is unrelated to the target intervention: liquid-metal dealloying of a directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h.

It assumes interdiffusion-driven W–Cu phase separation and voiding without evidence; the target mechanism instead involves preferential Ti dissolution, Cu replacement, retention of RHEA ligaments, and spontaneous formation of a W-rich passivating interlayer.
None of the cited evidence supports ALD Nb coatings on W–Cu interfaces or demonstrates improved thermal conductivity from such a coating.
Processing temperature, duration, architecture, thermal-test range, and irradiation dose and energy are unspecified, preventing comparison with the target conditions.
The irradiation claim is extrapolated to the composite despite no identified evidence or defined irradiation protocol.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad fusion-joint context and proposes a testable coated-versus-untreated comparison, but it does not reconstruct the material, intervention, mechanism, or quantitative outcomes of the target study. The target produced aligned, bicontinuous RHEA–Cu through selective liquid-metal dealloying, including an approximately 300 nm W-rich interlayer and strong high-temperature conductivity gains. The generated answer instead introduces an unsupported Nb ALD barrier and gives only generic service conditions and outcomes. E1–E2 establish the general W/CuCrZr joint challenge, while E3–E4 concern coated diamond composites and cannot validate Nb-coated W–Cu. The proposed experiment has moderate discriminating value, but it needs specified coating thickness, consolidation route, temperature and irradiation conditions, independent thermal-only and irradiation tests, and a falsification criterion that does not require both structural and conductivity endpoints to fail simultaneously.
